tasks.short: Approve payment requests that sit above the bookkeepers' mandate.

today.trigger: A bookkeeper routes a disbursement the mandate does not let them release: a supplier invoice, a flex-agency invoice, a credit note, or a one-off payment request.
steps: Open the AFAS workflow item and the PDF invoice or request.
Check the purchase order, goods receipt, cost centre, VAT code and whether the amount sits inside policy.
For a flex-agency invoice, compare hours and rates with the agency portal, usually by retyping totals into Excel.
Send gaps back to the site or the bookkeeper, or approve and record the coding.
Co-sign the SEPA batch that AFAS sends to Rabobank.
drudgery: Opening invoices the match already explains
Re-keying agency hours into a side sheet
Chasing Tilburg, Venlo and Rotterdam for a missing receipt
Ticking duplicates and VAT codes one by one
today.time_sinks: Most of the 147 hours sit in exceptions and in agency invoices that do not match the portal, plus waiting on site managers before a batch can be released.

lenses.faster: The match to order, receipt, mandate, VAT, duplicate and IBAN is finished before the item reaches the controller, so the queue is the failures only. Coding and the policy clause travel with the item, and the retyping into Excel drops out.
lenses.autonomous: An in-policy invoice that matches posts to the ledger and joins the payment proposal when the receipt is booked, with no daily prompt to the controller. A failed rule opens a task on its own.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost Noordhaven would tie every agency line to portal hours and every warehouse receipt to the invoice in the same week, including the small invoices that now pass unread.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss confirming a match the system has already made. What remains is a real dispute: a haulier rate, a damaged delivery, a site that ordered outside the contract.
lenses.options: Each exception arrives with the treatments the mandate allows, such as pay, split across site cost centres, hold for a receipt, or return, each with the euro effect and the policy line.
lenses.altitude: The controller maintains the mandate matrix, the match tolerances and the weekly sample of auto-released payments, and stops clearing items the rules already cover.
reach: The bookkeepers' exception coding on purchase invoices
First-line review of the three agencies' weekly invoices
The accountant's accrual for received-not-invoiced warehouse deliveries

tasks.human_edge: Noticing a request that passes the written rules and is still wrong: a changed IBAN on a known haulier, a May volume spike that the shifts do not support, or a site manager approving spend they raised themselves.
tasks.pattern_why: The check is a rule, but the money moves only after a recorded decision, and agency PDFs, missing receipts and new suppliers are genuine exceptions. An agent can assemble the evidence across AFAS, the portals and Rabobank; a person clears what failed before it enters the batch.

in_practice.trigger: An invoice or payment request is booked in AFAS, or a nightly match job flags an agency invoice against the portal export.
steps: AFAS pulls the order, receipt, supplier, VAT code and mandate limit.
Rules test three-way match, duplicate, VAT, cost-centre rights and whether the IBAN equals the master record.
Flex invoices are matched to the agency export of hours and agreed rates.
Clean items inside mandate post and enter the payment proposal. Exceptions open a task with the failed rule and the policy line.
The controller decides the exception. A second authorised person releases the Rabobank batch.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller decides every exception, every supplier IBAN change and a weekly sample of auto-released payments. A different authorised user releases the SEPA batch in Rabobank.
data_needed: Written mandate matrix by amount, cost centre and site
Open purchase orders and goods receipts
Supplier master IBANs and VAT numbers
Agency hour and rate exports
Policy clauses for non-PO spend
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS workflow log, kept with the weekly sample so the external auditor can re-perform the match.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit can route a purchase invoice, match it to an order and a receipt, and build a payment proposal from approved items.
evidence.source: AFAS Profit purchase-to-pay and payment proposal (named product, model knowledge)

evidence.claim: Rabobank business banking accepts SEPA batches and returns statements that a ledger can import.
evidence.source: Rabobank Business Banking batch payments and CAMT/MT940 statements (named product, model knowledge)

evidence.claim: A large share of Dutch mid-market invoice fraud is a changed supplier IBAN sent by mail, so the IBAN check has to stay outside the invoice approval itself.
evidence.source: model knowledge

risks: Auto-release without a mandate the Finance Director has signed, and without a stored sample, will fail the four-eyes test the auditor expects.
An IBAN change that rides inside an invoice approval is the usual payment-fraud path; it has to stay a separate dual-controlled master-data change.
Agency PDFs name individual flex workers. That file stays in AFAS and the tenant, under AVG, and does not go into a public chat tool.
Inlenersbeloning disputes are an HR and CAO question. Finance can flag a rate that does not match the contract and should not invent the legal rate.
research_questions: In the last quarter, what share of items the controller approved were inside a written mandate and a clean three-way match?
Where is a supplier IBAN changed today, and can that change be entered from the same screen as the invoice approval?
Can each of the three agency portals produce an hour-and-rate export AFAS can match, or only a PDF?
What mandate thresholds and cost-centre rights are actually written down, and who last signed them?

tasks.short: Watch cash, reserves and whether filings are on track.

today.trigger: Each morning, and again before payroll, VAT and the large supplier runs, the controller checks whether the company can pay and whether a filing is due.
steps: Read the Rabobank balance, the AFAS liquidity screen and the Power BI cash page from last night's extract.
Lay payroll, loonheffing, pension, VAT and known supplier runs next to the balance in Excel.
Tick the filing calendar for BTW, ICP, loonheffing, pension premiums and the annual accounts.
Compare doubtful-debt, claims, holiday-allowance and absence-insurance reserves with the floors the controller keeps in a sheet.
Mail the Finance Director if the balance or a reserve looks short.
drudgery: Copying the same balances from Rabobank, AFAS and Power BI into one sheet
Asking colleagues whether a return was actually filed
Rebuilding a four-week cash view that was already built last week
today.time_sinks: The nightly Power BI extract is a day behind the bank, so the controller rebuilds today's position by hand whenever payroll or a large agency payment is close.

lenses.faster: Balances, due filings and reserve floors land on one page before the morning starts. The copy-paste between Rabobank, AFAS and Excel drops out, and only an amber line needs a look.
lenses.autonomous: A scheduled check runs after the bank statement import and after the nightly AFAS refresh. It pages the controller only when cash, a covenant or a filing date breaches a written floor.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost Noordhaven would watch cash by site and by the next payroll, VAT and agency cycle every day, with the holiday-allowance accrual and the flex season included as standard lines.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss rebuilding the cash sheet. What remains is the judgement on whether a reserve is honestly large enough, and the call to the Finance Director when it is not.
lenses.options: The morning page shows the base cash path and two named stresses, a late top-ten customer and a peak-flex week, with the euro gap to the cash floor on each.
lenses.altitude: The controller sets the floors, the filing calendar and what counts as a breach, and reviews the breach log, rather than assembling the position each morning.
reach: The credit officer's expected receipts for the next two weeks
The payroll specialist's calendar of net pay, loonheffing and pension payments
The bookkeepers' view of supplier payments already promised but not yet in the batch

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a reserve is enough when the number is a claim, a bad debt or an absence case, and deciding when a short-term dip is still inside the Rabobank facility.
tasks.pattern_why: Balances, due dates and written floors are structured, and the result is a pass or a fail that a second person can re-perform. A model is not required to compare Rabobank, AFAS and the filing calendar. A breach opens a task; it does not move money.

in_practice.trigger: The Rabobank statement import finishes, the nightly AFAS refresh finishes, or a filing date is inside its warning window.
steps: Import the statement and compare it with the AFAS bank journal.
Roll forward known outflows: payroll, loonheffing, pension, VAT, agency invoices and the holiday-allowance run.
Compare cash and reserves with the written floors and the facility headroom.
Mark each statutory filing as not due, prepared, filed or late, from the calendar and the filing log.
Open a task to the controller only on a breach, with the figures and the floor that failed.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller reviews every breach and any change to a floor or to the filing calendar. Quiet days need no sign-off. Moving money or filing a return stays on its own approval path.
data_needed: Written cash minimum and any Rabobank covenant numbers
Filing calendar with owner and due date
Reserve policy with floors for debt, claims, holiday allowance and absence
Payroll and tax payment dates
Open customer receipts from AFAS accounts receivable
in_practice.logs_to: A daily control log in AFAS or SharePoint with the figures, the floor and the breach decision, kept for the audit file.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit shows bank journals, liquidity and open receivables and payables from the same ledger Noordhaven already uses.
evidence.source: AFAS Profit financial administration (named product, model knowledge)

evidence.claim: Rabobank provides same-day statement files that accounting systems import, which is more current than a nightly dashboard extract.
evidence.source: Rabobank Business Banking statements (named product, model knowledge)

evidence.claim: Power BI on a nightly AFAS extract cannot by itself show this morning's bank balance.
evidence.source: model knowledge, applied to the Noordhaven setup given in the brief

risks: A green dashboard built on last night's extract will be wrong on payroll morning. The bank statement has to be the cash source.
Reserve floors that are only a habit in someone's sheet will either false-alarm every week or never alarm.
Filing status typed in by the same person who files is a weak control. The log should record the filing reference from the Belastingdienst or the pension fund.
Covenant calculations often use definitions that differ from the management cash figure. Those definitions have to be in the rule before anyone trusts the alert.
research_questions: Is there a written cash minimum, reserve floor and Rabobank covenant formula, with numbers a check can apply?
How many items on the compliance list are fixed filing dates, and how many are estimates a person must remake each month?
How often does the morning Rabobank balance differ from the Power BI cash page by enough to change a payment decision?
Which filing or payment was late in the last two years, and would a date check have shown it in time?

tasks.short: Judge whether to draw the Rabobank line or place surplus.

today.trigger: A large outflow is coming, the balance sits above the operating need, or the Finance Director asks whether to draw or repay the facility.
steps: Build a cash forecast from AFAS open items, the payroll calendar, agency orders and the Rabobank balance.
Estimate the holiday-allowance payout, VAT settlement and the flex peak from last year's pattern plus this year's orders.
Compare the low point with the undrawn Rabobank facility and the cash floor.
Write a short recommendation to draw, repay or leave the surplus on the current account.
Discuss it with the Finance Director before anyone calls the bank.
drudgery: Stitching payroll, tax, agencies and customers into one weekly sheet
Updating the same forecast three times because a site changed its order book
Formatting the recommendation mail
today.time_sinks: The forecast is rebuilt from scratch more than weekly because there is no single driver model, and agency orders for the next month arrive late and in three different layouts.

lenses.faster: The 13-week drivers refresh from AFAS, Rabobank and the agency orders before the controller looks at them. Collecting the opening balance and the known outflows drops out of the morning.
lenses.autonomous: A refresh runs when the bank statement imports or when payroll releases its payment calendar, and it puts the revised low point on the controller's desk without a reminder.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost the company would keep a living 13-week forecast by site, including flex season and the holiday-allowance payout, and would use it every week rather than only when cash looks tight.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss pasting subledgers into the cash sheet. What remains is the recommendation itself and the conversation with the Finance Director and the bank.
lenses.options: Each recommendation carries a base path, a late-customer path and a peak-flex path, with the draw or the surplus under each and the week the floor breaks.
lenses.altitude: The controller owns the driver model and the treasury limits, and reviews where last month's forecast was wrong, rather than rebuilding the sheet for each request.
reach: The FP&A analysts' short-term cash bridge, which today sits apart from the monthly forecast
A prepared brief for the Finance Director's call with Rabobank
The credit officer's collection priorities, ranked by what they do to the low point

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what the company is willing to tell the bank, and whether a surplus should stay liquid because a customer or a site lease is shakier than the sheet shows.
tasks.pattern_why: The forecast can be assembled by rules, but the recommendation commits the company to the bank and sits with the Finance Director. The controller keeps the lead; the model prepares the paths and the gaps. This is amplify work: the judgement stays, the assembly shrinks.

in_practice.trigger: The cash monitor shows the low point inside four weeks of the floor, a surplus above the placement threshold, or the Finance Director asks for a recommendation.
steps: Refresh the 13-week model from open receivables, open payables, the payroll calendar, VAT due and agency orders.
Add the holiday-allowance run and the planned flex peak as explicit drivers.
Compute base, late-customer and peak-flex lows against the facility headroom and the treasury limits.
Draft the recommendation in the company's words: draw, repay, place on deposit, or wait, with the assumption that moves the answer.
The controller edits and signs it. The Finance Director sends anything that instructs the bank.
in_practice.human_gate: No draw, repayment or placement goes to Rabobank without the Finance Director. The controller signs the recommendation and the assumptions. The model does not write to the bank.
data_needed: Treasury limits: allowed instruments, tenors and who may instruct the bank
Facility limit, drawn amount, interest and covenant headroom
13-week drivers from AFAS and the payroll calendar
Agency order book for the coming weeks
Last year's holiday-allowance payout date and amount
in_practice.logs_to: The signed recommendation and the forecast version are stored in SharePoint next to the treasury limits, and the actual cash is compared with the forecast four weeks later.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit and Rabobank already hold the open items, the bank balance and the payment calendar this forecast needs.
evidence.source: AFAS Profit and Rabobank Business Banking (named products, model knowledge)

evidence.claim: A 13-week direct cash forecast from drivers is standard treasury practice and can be built in the ledger or in a controlled workbook.
evidence.source: model knowledge

evidence.claim: Employers under CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer pay an annual holiday allowance that is large enough to move cash in the payout month.
evidence.source: model knowledge of the transport CAO

risks: A recommendation that places surplus outside what the articles and the treasury limits allow creates a governance breach even if the maths is right.
Flex orders that arrive late will dominate the error. A precise model on stale agency numbers is false comfort.
The controller and the Finance Director must stay the only people who can instruct a draw. A draft mail to the bank should not be one click from send.
Covenant definitions and 'cash' in the forecast are often different. The recommendation has to use the covenant definition when headroom is the point.
research_questions: Do the articles of association or a treasury policy limit surplus to Rabobank deposits, and who may sign a drawdown?
How many weeks ahead are customer receipts, payroll, VAT and the three agencies' orders known with an error the facility can absorb?
Would a better forecast have changed a real draw, placement or payment delay in the last year?
In which month is the holiday allowance paid for transport staff and for warehouse staff, and how large was it last year?

tasks.short: Steer the budget, the big purchases and the investment proposals.

today.trigger: The annual budget round starts, a site asks for equipment or extra flex, or a quarterly reforecast is due.
steps: Issue the timetable and the templates to FP&A, the accountants and the three site managers.
Chase Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo for volume, headcount, overtime and flex assumptions.
Review procurement commitments and investment proposals against the budget and the cash view.
Consolidate versions in Excel and sit with FP&A until the bridge explains.
Present the pack to the Finance Director and record the decisions.
drudgery: Merging site workbooks that do not use the same cost centres
Chasing version numbers by mail
Rebuilding the bridge after one site changes volume
today.time_sinks: The cycle slips on site assumptions and on meetings, not on the arithmetic. Consolidation and the story of the bridge take the rest of the 69 hours.

lenses.faster: Site submissions land on the AFAS cost-centre structure, the consolidation and the bridge calculate themselves, and the chase list is the missing owners only. Reformatting workbooks drops out.
lenses.autonomous: When a site misses the timetable, or a proposal arrives without a cost centre and a payback, a reminder goes to that owner with the gap named. The controller is pulled in when the gap stays open.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost Noordhaven would reforecast the three sites on the same drivers every quarter, and would cost a warehouse investment properly the first time, including flex, maintenance and cash.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss merging spreadsheets. What remains is the argument with a site manager about volume, and the decision on what the company can afford.
lenses.options: Each investment proposal comes with a low, base and high volume case and the effect on the year, the cash low point and the site result.
lenses.altitude: The controller designs the planning calendar, the driver definitions and the standard for a proposal, and reviews the quality of what the sites and FP&A submit.
reach: The FP&A analysts' first consolidation and variance bridge
A completeness check on purchase commitments that today falls between the bookkeepers and the sites
A first financial note on equipment proposals before they reach the Finance Director

tasks.human_edge: Hearing that a site's volume is a hope rather than booked work, and refusing to close the budget until that is said in the room with the site manager.
tasks.pattern_why: This task is directing people across a calendar. The pack, the bridge and the missing-owner list can be prepared; the controller still runs the round and stands behind what goes to the Finance Director. Software does not settle a site's volume assumption.

in_practice.trigger: The planning calendar reaches a budget, reforecast or investment deadline, or a proposal is submitted in SharePoint.
steps: Open the round with a locked chart of accounts, cost centres per site and a template filled from last year's actuals.
Collect site drivers: volume, own headcount, overtime, flex hours and rates, and capital spend.
Build the consolidated result, cash and headcount, and a bridge from the previous approved version.
Score each investment proposal for completeness: cost, timing, site, payback and whether works-council advice is required.
The controller reviews the bridge with FP&A and takes the open assumptions to the Finance Director.
in_practice.human_gate: The Finance Director approves the budget and any investment above the mandate. The controller approves the pack that is allowed into that meeting. A proposal that changes work in a warehouse is flagged for the works council route before it is treated as approved.
data_needed: Planning calendar and the owner of each input
Cost-centre map for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo
Actuals and the last approved budget from AFAS
Capital and flex proposals with timing
The threshold and the list of decisions that need works-council advice under the WOR
in_practice.logs_to: The approved version, the bridge and the decision log are stored in SharePoint, with the AFAS budget version they were loaded to.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit stores budgets and actuals on cost centres and can return the variances a consolidation needs.
evidence.source: AFAS Profit budget module and financial reporting (named product, model knowledge)

evidence.claim: Works-council advice or consent applies to some investments and regulations that change work, under the Wet op de ondernemingsraden.
evidence.source: model knowledge of WOR article 25 and article 27

evidence.claim: Version-controlled workbook consolidation is still the usual way Dutch mid-market controllers run a budget even when the ledger holds the actuals.
evidence.source: model knowledge

risks: Loading a budget into AFAS before the Finance Director has approved it makes the system look more certain than the decision.
A template that sites cannot fill will be bypassed with another Excel file, and the company will be back to three versions.
Treating a warehouse automation proposal as a finance-only decision skips the works council where the WOR requires advice.
FP&A already owns much of this cycle. Automating the pack and then having the controller redo it doubles the work.
research_questions: Which budget inputs are still free-format workbooks, and which cost centres do the sites actually recognise?
How much of these 69 hours is meetings and chasing, and how much is building the model?
Which investments in the last two years needed works-council advice, and was finance told before the order was placed?
What does the controller decide in this cycle that FP&A and the Finance Director do not already decide?

tasks.short: Tell the management team what a financial choice will cost.

today.trigger: The management team asks for a view before a decision, or the monthly meeting needs a financial note on policy, price, headcount or a site.
steps: Clarify the decision, the horizon and who is asking.
Pull actuals, the forecast and cash from Power BI and AFAS, then rebuild the piece that the dashboard does not cut.
Draft a note or a short slide with one recommended action.
Test the numbers with FP&A or the relevant accountant.
Talk the Finance Director and the management team through the choice and the open risk.
drudgery: Rebuilding a cut of the ledger the dashboard does not have
Formatting slides from a workbook
Repeating the same caveat about forecast quality in every meeting
today.time_sinks: The hours go to hunting for a reliable cut of revenue, labour and flex by site, and to rewriting the note so the management team will recognise the operation in it.

lenses.faster: The first note arrives with the actuals, the forecast, the cash effect and the last time the company made a similar choice. Hunting the ledger and rebuilding the slide from scratch drops out.
lenses.autonomous: Before each management meeting the pack refreshes from AFAS and lists the decisions that are actually open, without someone remembering to start a deck.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost every management meeting would start from a one-page view the sites recognise: result, cash, forecast accuracy and the three choices that need a decision that month.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss rebuilding the deck. What remains is the conversation: what the company should do, and which number the controller will stand behind.
lenses.options: A request produces three actions, each with the effect on the month's result, on cash and on days sales outstanding, written so the meeting can choose one.
lenses.altitude: The controller sets what a decision note must contain and reviews whether past advice was followed and was right, rather than writing each note from a blank page.
reach: The FP&A analysts' monthly commentary for the sites
A first draft of the Finance Director's note to the management team
A cash and DSO reading of a large customer term-change that the credit officer is negotiating

tasks.human_edge: Saying in the room which figure is solid and which is a guess, and keeping the recommendation standing when a site director disputes it.
tasks.pattern_why: Advice is the controller's relationship with the management team. A model can prepare the cuts and the options; it cannot carry the advice. The person stays the lead, which matches amplify rather than automate.

in_practice.trigger: A management-team agenda is set, or a director asks the controller for a view on a specific choice.
steps: Frame the decision, the horizon, the sites affected and the metric that will move: result, cash, DSO or close risk.
Pull actuals and the latest forecast from AFAS, and show forecast accuracy on that line over recent months.
Draft three options with the euro effect and the assumption each one depends on.
The controller edits the recommendation and marks what is uncertain.
The controller, with the Finance Director where the choice is material, talks it through in the meeting and records the decision.
in_practice.human_gate: Nothing is advice to the management team until the controller signs the note. The Finance Director leads any choice that changes policy, the facility or the year's result. The model does not present.
data_needed: The decision asked, the horizon and the sites
Actuals and forecast by the lines the choice moves
Recent forecast accuracy on those lines
Open cash and DSO effects
Prior decisions on the same topic and what then happened
in_practice.logs_to: The signed note and the decision are stored in SharePoint and linked to the forecast version they used.

evidence.claim: Power BI and AFAS can supply the actuals, the cash and the DSO that a decision note is built from, when the model is on those sources.
evidence.source: Microsoft Power BI and AFAS Profit, both already in use at Noordhaven

evidence.claim: A fixed one-page decision note with options is a management practice, not a product, and it depends on the management team agreeing to use it.
evidence.source: model knowledge

risks: A fluent note on weak forecast accuracy will be trusted too early. The note has to show the recent error on that line.
Advice that commits the company in writing can become a policy. Drafts should stay in the working file until the controller signs.
Site-level labour figures can identify small teams. The pack for the management team should use the cuts HR and the works council already accept.
If the Finance Director and the controller both rewrite the same pack, the company has added a step.
research_questions: Which decisions in the last six months actually changed because of the controller's advice?
On which lines does the management team currently dispute the forecast, and what do they use instead?
How much of the advice depends on facts that are not in AFAS, such as a customer about to leave or a lease negotiation?
Will the management team read a one-page options note, or do they expect a presentation from the Finance Director only?

tasks.short: Budget pension, absence cover and casualty premiums against headcount.

today.trigger: The broker renews a policy, a premium invoice arrives, the budget round asks for employer costs, or a regulation changes the pension or absence scheme.
steps: Collect premium invoices and renewal notes for pension, verzuim insurance, WGA, fleet, cargo and warehouse cover.
Tie employer pension and social charges to the AFAS wage bill and headcount with the payroll specialist.
Ask Compensation and Benefits what changed in the schemes and what the works council has to consent to.
Build the year's cost, including the holiday-allowance effect on pensionable pay, in Excel.
Put the number into the budget and explain movements to the Finance Director.
drudgery: Reconciling a broker's PDF to headcount by hand
Separating transport-CAO staff from warehouse-CAO staff when the invoice does not
Retyping premium tables into the budget workbook
today.time_sinks: The slow part is understanding what an invoice covers, and waiting on the broker, the pension fund and Compensation and Benefits for a split the ledger does not hold.

lenses.faster: Premium invoices are read into a standard table and tied to AFAS headcount and wage-bill totals before the controller opens them. The retyping and the hunt for which CAO a premium belongs to drop out.
lenses.autonomous: A renewal date or a premium invoice that differs from the accrued cost opens a task for the controller and for Compensation and Benefits, without a diary reminder.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost the company would see employer cost per site and per CAO every month, and would price a flex peak's effect on absence insurance and agency cost before the season starts.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss cross-adding broker PDFs. What remains is the judgement on a premium increase, and the conversation about whether claims and absence are actually changing.
lenses.options: A renewal is shown as three covers: renew as quoted, change the excess, or self-fund a larger slice, with the budget and cash effect of each and the claims history underneath.
lenses.altitude: The controller sets how employer cost is classified and reviewed, and checks that premiums, accruals and headcount still tie, rather than building the workbook each renewal.
reach: The Compensation and Benefits Specialist's cost estimate at renewal
The payroll specialist's premium journals for pension and social charges
A check that agency invoices do not quietly carry insurance elements the company also accrues

tasks.human_edge: Seeing whether a premium rise is the market or the company's own absence and claims, and knowing which changes need the works council before anyone puts them in the budget.
tasks.pattern_why: The tie from premium to headcount is a rule, but scheme design, a broker negotiation and works-council consent sit with Compensation and Benefits and with management. The controller should get a sourced cost pack and still own the number that enters the budget. Individual absence files stay with HR.

in_practice.trigger: A premium invoice or a renewal lands in the mailbox, or the budget calendar asks for employer costs.
steps: Extract the premium, the period, the cover and the headcount basis from the invoice into a fixed table.
Compare it with AFAS totals for headcount and pensionable wage, split by the transport CAO and the warehouse CAO, with no individual health data.
Flag a variance above tolerance and any quote that changes an employee contribution or a scheme rule.
Draft the budget bridge and, at renewal, the three cover options with cash timing.
The controller agrees the accrual and the budget figure. Compensation and Benefits owns the scheme and the works-council route.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller signs the cost that enters the budget and the accrual. Any change to an employee contribution, pension or other personnel regulation waits for Compensation and Benefits and, where the WOR requires it, works-council consent. The controller does not see diagnosis or Wet verbetering poortwachter files.
data_needed: Premium invoices and the cover register
AFAS headcount and wage-bill totals by CAO and site
Accrual accounts for pension, social charges, holiday allowance and insurance
Renewal dates and current excesses
A list of scheme changes that require works-council consent
in_practice.logs_to: The tie-out between invoice, headcount total and accrual is stored in the close file in SharePoint, without named absence or health data.

evidence.claim: AFAS Payroll already holds headcount, wage components and the journals for pension and employer charges that a premium tie-out needs.
evidence.source: AFAS Payroll and the general ledger in AFAS Profit (named product, model knowledge)

evidence.claim: Dutch employer cost in this sector is pension, employer levies, verzuim and WGA cover, and fleet, cargo and warehouse insurance, not a US-style employer health plan.
evidence.source: model knowledge of Dutch payroll and the transport sector

evidence.claim: Works councils have consent rights on a number of personnel regulations, including many benefit rules, under the WOR.
evidence.source: model knowledge of WOR article 27

risks: Health and absence data are special-category data under the AVG. A cost pack built from named cases, or from Wet verbetering poortwachter files, is the wrong design. Totals are enough.
Putting a scheme change into the budget before works-council consent, where consent is required, creates a labour-relations problem the forecast then has to unwind.
This O*NET task overlaps Compensation and Benefits and Payroll. Automating it inside finance can duplicate their work or, worse, move scheme design onto the controller.
A model that recommends cutting an individual benefit, or that scores employees, is the wrong tool and can fall under the EU AI Act employment provisions. Keep it on aggregate cost.
Casualty policies renew on broker wording that a table can misread. The controller still opens a renewal that changes exclusions or limits.
research_questions: Which of these costs does the controller build today, and which already sit with Compensation and Benefits or Payroll?
Is the warehouse CAO in the same pension fund as the transport CAO, and can both premiums be tied to an AFAS wage total?
Can the broker's invoices be checked against headcount totals without any named absence or medical data?
Which premium changes in the last renewal actually required works-council consent?

tasks.short: Check payroll deductions and the wage journal before pay goes out.

today.trigger: Payroll finishes the monthly run, or a correction run, and the wage journal and the payment batches need a finance check before money leaves.
steps: Take the AFAS payroll totals for loonheffing, pension, attachments and other deductions.
Compare the loonjournaalpost with the payroll summary and with last month, often in Excel.
Check that the net-pay batch, the loonheffing payment and the pension payment add back to the journal.
Question overtime, shift allowances and holiday-allowance accruals that jumped versus headcount.
Sign off, or send corrections back to the payroll specialist, then let the batches go to Rabobank and the Belastingdienst.
drudgery: Rebuilding a tie-out AFAS already calculated
Copying component totals into a workbook to see the movement
Chasing an explanation for a difference that is a known parameter change
today.time_sinks: The time goes to movements nobody has explained, to corrections after the journal was posted, and to flex-agency cost being discussed in the same review even though those workers are not on this payroll.

lenses.faster: The tie-out between the payroll summary, the loonjournaalpost and the three outgoing payments is ready when the run closes. Rebuilding it in Excel drops out, and the controller reads the variances that failed a rule.
lenses.autonomous: Closing the payroll run starts the tie-out on its own. A clean run waits for the existing release. A broken tie, a new deduction code or a swing against headcount opens a task before anyone is asked.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost every run would show, by site and CAO, that gross-to-net, pension, loonheffing and the accrual for holiday allowance agree, and corrections would be rare enough to explain one by one.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss the side spreadsheet. What remains is a real payroll question: a new allowance, a loonbeslag, a parameter the CAO change actually requires.
lenses.options: A failed tie shows the two or three plausible causes, such as a late joiner, a correction run or a parameter change, each with the people-count and the euro amount, for payroll to confirm.
lenses.altitude: The controller owns the tie-out rules and the list of deduction codes the ledger accepts, and samples runs, rather than recomputing what AFAS Payroll has already computed.
reach: The payroll specialist's journal check, as a reviewer rather than a second calculator
The accountant's monthly wage reconciliation in the close
A clear split so agency invoices stay in accounts payable and out of the wage tie-out

tasks.human_edge: Knowing when a movement is a CAO or parameter change that should hit everyone's pay, and when it is a single employee matter that payroll and HR must handle in private.
tasks.pattern_why: AFAS already computes and withholds. What finance adds is a check that structured totals agree: summary, journal, net pay, loonheffing and pension. That check has a right answer and does not need a language model. A person sees the exceptions and the release stays on the current signature path.

in_practice.trigger: The payroll specialist sets the run to calculated in AFAS, before the net-pay batch and the loonheffing payment are released.
steps: Read the payroll component totals, headcount and the draft loonjournaalpost from AFAS.
Tie gross-to-net, each deduction code, the journal and the payment batches to the cent.
Compare pension, loonheffing and net pay with last month per FTE, split by CAO and site.
Hold the release if a code is new, a tie fails, or a swing exceeds the tolerance. Pass a clean run through the existing signature.
Post the journal to the ledger only after that release, and store the tie-out with the run.
in_practice.human_gate: The payroll specialist remains responsible for the calculation and for employee-level corrections. The controller, or the person who already co-signs, releases a run that failed a tie or breached tolerance. A clean run follows the signature path already in use. No model recalculates tax.
systems: AFAS Profit payroll and general ledger
data_needed: AFAS component totals and the loonjournaalpost
Payment batches for net pay, loonheffing and pension
Headcount and FTE by site and CAO
The list of allowed deduction codes and the variance tolerance
Parameter changes logged by payroll for the period
in_practice.logs_to: The tie-out result is stored with the AFAS payroll run number, so the close and the auditor can see who released an exception.

evidence.claim: AFAS Payroll calculates Dutch wage tax and social deductions, produces the loonjournaalpost and can prepare the related payments.
evidence.source: AFAS Payroll (named product, model knowledge)

evidence.claim: The Belastingdienst wage-tax tables are applied by certified payroll software; a second calculation in a language model would be a worse source than AFAS.
evidence.source: model knowledge

evidence.claim: Flex workers hired through staffing agencies are invoiced to the client and are not, by default, on the client's wage tax return.
evidence.source: model knowledge of Dutch agency hiring and payrolling

risks: A second calculator beside AFAS will drift from the official tables and create false differences. The control is a tie-out, not a recomputation.
Posting a wrong journal, or releasing net pay early, hits about a thousand people at once. Exception release stays with a named person.
Loonbeslag and other employee-level deductions are sensitive personal data. The finance view uses totals and codes, not the underlying court documents.
If any flex workers are in fact on Noordhaven's payroll, a control that assumes they are all agency invoices will miss them.
A tool that decided an individual's deduction could fall under the EU AI Act's employment provisions. This design does not decide deductions; AFAS and the CAO parameters do.
research_questions: Which deductions does AFAS already compute, and which does finance still adjust in Excel?
How many corrections follow a normal month after the loonjournaalpost is posted, and what causes them?
Who signs the net-pay batch and the loonheffing payment today, and where does the controller sit on that path?
Are all 150 to 300 flex workers billed by the agencies, or are some on Noordhaven's own payroll?

tasks.short: Get the monthly statements, the forecast and the filings out.

today.trigger: The month ends, a filing falls due, or the Finance Director asks for the forecast and the management pack.
steps: Chase the accountants for reconciliations: bank, VAT, payroll, agencies, goods received not invoiced, and the three sites' cut-off.
Review accruals for holiday allowance, claims, doubtful debts and flex hours worked but not yet invoiced.
Direct FP&A on the forecast and read the flux in the Power BI pack, then rebuild what the nightly extract got wrong.
Draft or edit the commentary and the statements for the Finance Director.
Prepare or review BTW, ICP and, once a year, the jaarrekening pack for the auditor and the KvK filing.
drudgery: Chasing status of reconciliations by mail
Copying ledger totals into a close workbook
Rewriting flux comments that say a balance 'moved because it moved'
today.time_sinks: The close waits on cut-off from the warehouses, on agency invoices for the last days of the month, and on commentary that is rewritten because the first pack came from last night's extract rather than the closed ledger.

lenses.faster: Reconciliations, flux and the statement pack generate from the closed AFAS ledger. The controller edits commentary and estimates instead of collecting workbooks, and the copy into Excel drops out.
lenses.autonomous: The close calendar opens each task when the previous one finishes. A reconciliation that does not tie, or a flux over the threshold, opens a named task without a chase mail.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost Noordhaven would close every month to the same standard as year-end, with a forecast the site managers recognise and an audit file that is the close file, not a separate spring project.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss the chase mails and the close workbook. What remains is the estimate: is the accrual honest, and does the forecast describe the warehouses the managers actually run.
lenses.options: Material accruals and forecast lines come with a low and a high, and the effect of each on the month's result and on the cash view, before the controller picks the figure that will be published.
lenses.altitude: The controller designs the close calendar, the tie thresholds and the definition of a finished month, then signs the pack and improves whatever the auditor or the sites still correct.
reach: The accountants' standard lead sheets and flux on recurring balance-sheet accounts
The FP&A analysts' first forecast refresh in the same pack as the actuals
The audit request list, produced from the close log rather than assembled in spring

tasks.human_edge: Signing the month: which accrual is fair, which site's forecast is wishful, and what the management team should believe. The auditor and the Belastingdienst need that signature from a person.
tasks.pattern_why: The pack is several steps across subledgers, with exceptions at cut-off, agencies and estimates. Rules and a workflow can prepare it. The month counts only when the controller approves it, and statutory filings stay on the existing signature. That is automate-class production with a gate, not an unmanned close.

in_practice.trigger: The last working day of the month closes, or a BTW, ICP or annual-accounts deadline enters its preparation window.
steps: Lock the task list: bank, VAT, payroll tie-out, agency accrual, goods received not invoiced, inter-site cut-off and the recurring accruals.
Import ties from AFAS and mark each as tied, explained or open, using the live ledger rather than the nightly Power BI extract.
Draft the statements, the flux over threshold and a first commentary, with low and high on material estimates.
The controller reviews open items and estimates, then signs the management pack for the Finance Director.
Filing files for BTW, ICP and the annual accounts are prepared from that signed ledger and follow the current review before anyone files.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller signs every monthly pack before it goes to the management team. The Finance Director signs the annual accounts. Tax filings go out only through the person who files them today. An open tie above tolerance cannot be waived by the workflow.
data_needed: Close calendar with owner and day
AFAS trial balance and subledgers after cut-off
Tie thresholds and the list of recurring accruals
Forecast version from FP&A on the same chart of accounts
Filing deadlines and the signed status of BTW, ICP and the jaarrekening
in_practice.logs_to: The close log in SharePoint, linked to the AFAS period lock, with each tie, each waived item and the controller's sign-off, so the audit file is the same log.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit produces the trial balance, subledgers and financial statements from the ledger Noordhaven already keeps.
evidence.source: AFAS Profit financial reporting (named product, model knowledge)

evidence.claim: A nightly Power BI extract is a weak source for the close pack on the days the ledger is still moving.
evidence.source: model knowledge, applied to the Noordhaven setup in the brief

evidence.claim: Dutch companies of this scale file BTW and, where they have intra-EU movements, ICP listings, and they publish annual accounts that an auditor can be required to audit.
evidence.source: model knowledge of Dutch filing practice

risks: Signing a pack sourced from Power BI rather than the locked period will recreate the audit adjustments the close is meant to avoid.
An agent that books accruals on its own will put estimates into the ledger without the controller's judgement. Draft the entry; a person posts it.
BTW and ICP errors carry penalties. The filing step stays with the person who is responsible for it now.
Warehouse cut-off and late agency invoices dominate the real close time. Automating the commentary does not move those.
Management packs that show individual productivity can become a works-council issue. Publish the same site totals the company already shares.
research_questions: How many working days does the close take now, and which reconciliations are still done in Excel?
What were last year's audit adjustments, by amount and by cause, especially cut-off, accruals and classification?
Which outputs are management reports, and which are filings to the Belastingdienst, Statistics Netherlands or the KvK?
Does the forecast the sites say they trust use the same cost centres as the AFAS actuals?

role.altitude: The controller becomes the person who designs how Noordhaven closes, pays and forecasts: the mandate, the tie-out rules, the cash floors and the standard for a decision note. The month, the batch and the budget pack are produced by those rules. The controller signs what counts, fixes what the rules get wrong, and tells the management team what the figures mean.
reach: The bookkeepers' exception invoices and the coding quality that slows the close
The accountants' recurring lead sheets and the wage-journal tie-out at month end
The FP&A analysts' first forecast refresh and the cash bridge, on the same definitions as the actuals
The credit officer's next-two-weeks receipts, read as part of the cash low point
The payroll specialist's payment calendar and the premium journals, reviewed from totals
The Compensation and Benefits cost bridge at renewal, without taking over scheme design
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks are about 725 hours of a full controller year, so a large part of the role sits outside this list. What does not compress is the signature: the monthly pack, the tax filing, the payment release and the advice in the management meeting. Provisions, Rabobank headroom and a dispute with a site manager stay with a person. Payroll calculation and benefit design stay with Payroll and Compensation and Benefits; pulling them onto the controller would break the split of duties. One controller cannot also be the second pair of eyes on their own release.
skills_to_grow: Writing mandate rules, match tolerances and close ties so an auditor can re-perform them
Reading the AFAS invoice flow, the loonjournaalpost and the period lock, and stopping the side workbooks
A 13-week cash model with payroll, VAT, agencies, customers and the holiday-allowance run
Enough Titel 9 and wage-tax calendar knowledge to challenge a filing the accountant has prepared
Working with the Finance Director and the works council on which controls may run unattended
Sampling auto-released payments and clean payroll runs, and writing down what the sample found
role.ambitious_version: Noordhaven closes on a short, known calendar, from the locked AFAS ledger, with a forecast the three sites recognise and will defend. Invoices inside the mandate go through to a Rabobank batch that a second person releases, and the controller sees the exceptions, the IBAN changes and a sample. Cash shows the next payroll, the agency peak, VAT and the holiday-allowance payout before they hit the bank. The management team gets options with a number attached, and the audit file is the close log they already signed.
